concepts.why: Biblical-theological / secular: the name says the heavens opened and visions of God; Isaiah 6:1 and Zechariah 1:8 say only 'I saw' (Isaiah 6:1 is covered by the throne concept, Zechariah 1:8 by the horses and 'What are these, my lord?').

Visions rule (connect, do not interpret): the concept is meant to hold every explanation the texts themselves give, and it now holds some (Daniel 7:17, 8:20-21, Revelation 17:15) while leaving out the angel's own explanations of the fourth beast and of the seven heads and ten horns. A selective set of the texts' interpretations is itself a choice. Quoting them takes no side on what they refer to; omitting them looks like hiding obvious links.
Secular / literary: Isaiah 6:5 is a cry of ruin, not a falling facedown; the other six passages fall on their faces or are raised up.
Biblical-theological: 'Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?' names no host standing by Him; the passage says a plural 'Us' and the name would be asking the reader to supply the host.

concepts.name: A rainbow in a cloud
concepts.why: Copyright / the BSB's words: 'The bow in the cloud' is the KJV's phrase for Genesis 9:13; the BSB and the notes read 'rainbow in the clouds' and 'rainbow in a cloud' (Ezekiel 1:28). Revelation 4:3 has the rainbow around the throne and 10:1 in a cloud, so the plain wording fits all four.

concepts.name: One like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader (original arbitrates): Daniel 7:13 reads 'like a son of man' with no article, and Revelation 1:13 and 14:14 likewise 'like a son of man' (no article) in the Greek. The BSB's capitalised 'the Son of Man' is already the title, so the name gives the title to Daniel before the texts do. Lower case keeps the words the texts have; the notes stay exact BSB quotations, and Matthew 24:30, 26:64 and Mark 13:26 keep their own 'the Son of Man'. The name makes no claim that one text is fulfilled in the other.

Secular / Jewish: Matthew 24:30 has the tribes mourning but nothing pierced and no looking on a pierced one; it is already in the previous concept. Zechariah 12:10, John 19:37 and Revelation 1:7 make the link in their own words (John says 'another Scripture', Revelation joins the two phrases).

Name against passages: both verses describe only the linen or robe and the golden belt or sash, not eyes or feet. Daniel 10:6 and Revelation 1:14-15 carry the shared words. Daniel 10:5 and Revelation 1:13 may go as a secondary concept (dressed in linen / robe, a belt or sash of gold).

concepts.name: The great Day of the LORD
concepts.why: Name against passages and all readers on 'soon': only Joel 1:15, Zephaniah 1:14 and Obadiah 15 say 'near'; Isaiah 13:9 says 'coming', Amos 5:18 and Malachi 3:2 do not say near at all, and Revelation 6:17 says the day 'has come'. 'Is near' therefore reads as the concept's claim about timing, which Revelation 6:17 contradicts in the same list. 'Great Day of the LORD' is in Joel 2:11, Zephaniah 1:14 and (as 'great day') Revelation 6:17.

Completeness, and the link the text itself makes: Revelation 13:2 names a leopard, a bear and a lion, the three beasts of Daniel 7:4-6 (the concept lists 7:3 and 7:7 only). Without them the leopard-bear-lion note in Revelation 13:2 has no partner.

Name against passages: the name is 'even if He does not', but Daniel 3:28, Daniel 6:22 and Hebrews 11:33-34 are all deliverance. Hebrews 11:35-38 (the others who were tortured, stoned, sawn in two) is the text's own 'even if He does not', and without it the concept shows only one half of Daniel 3:17-18.

Name against passages: Revelation 17:1 never names Babylon or its fall; the text's own link between the great prostitute and 'Babylon the great' is 17:5. Add it so the passage 17:1 stands on is shown.

Name against passages and Reformed / Catholic / secular: the cup in Revelation 17:4 is the woman's, full of abominations, not the cup of God's wrath; putting it under this name says her cup is His. Its link to Jeremiah 51:7 (a gold cup) can sit with the Babylon concept instead.

concepts.name: The harvest is ripe, the winepress is full
concepts.why: Name against passages: Isaiah 63:3, Revelation 14:19 and 19:15 are the winepress and have no sickle, so 'Swing Your sickle and reap' covers only half. Joel 3:13 has both in the texts' own words.
Name against passages: the name lists hail, but none of the Revelation passages given has hail (9:3 locusts, 16:2-4 sores and blood, 16:10 darkness). Revelation 16:21 and 8:7 are the hail.

concepts.name: Assembled for battle
note_fixes: Ezekiel 38:2: shares only the name Gog; replace with, or add, a verse that has the assembling (Ezekiel 38:7-9) so the passage holds the concept
concepts.why: Order of the last things and name against passages: 'The kings of the earth' fits only Psalm 2:2, Revelation 16:14 and 19:19; Joel 3:2, Zechariah 14:2 and Revelation 20:8 say the nations, and Ezekiel 38 says Gog. Gathering Revelation 16, 19 and 20 under 'the kings' lets a reader take them as one battle, which is exactly the point amillennial and premillennial readers part on. 'Assembled' and 'gathered' are the texts' own word for all of them and say nothing about whether they are one event or several.

concepts.name: The glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD
concepts.why: Name against passages: only Isaiah 6:4 and Revelation 15:8 say smoke; Exodus 40:34-35, 1 Kings 8:10-11 and Ezekiel 10:4 say cloud. 1 Kings 8:11's words fit all five (Isaiah 6:3-4 glory then smoke; Revelation 15:8 'smoke from the glory of God').

concepts.name: Books were opened, and one of them was the Book of Life
note_fixes: Daniel 12:1: the BSB has dashes where the note has ellipses ('your people-everyone whose name is found written in the book-will be delivered'); quote it exactly or cut at 'found written in the book'
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'The books were opened' is only Daniel 7:10 and Revelation 20:12; Exodus 32:32-33, Psalm 69:28, Malachi 3:16, Daniel 12:1, Revelation 3:5 and 20:15 are about being written in, or blotted out of, a book. Revelation 20:12 says both parts of the new name.

concepts.name: They will receive the kingdom and possess it forever
concepts.why: Israel and the church (Reformed, Baptist-dispensational, secular): 'The saints of the Most High' is Daniel's phrase and its referent is disputed; putting Luke 12:32 and Revelation 5:10 under it says the 'little flock' and those made a kingdom are Daniel's saints. The plain wording keeps Daniel 7:18's words without the identification, and Daniel 2:44 and Revelation 11:15 (God's kingdom, no saints named) then fit too.

concepts.name: I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me
concepts.why: Name against passages and Jewish / secular reader: Malachi 3:1, Isaiah 40:3 and Mark 1:2-3 do not say Elijah; the identification is Matthew 11:10-14 (and Luke 1:17), so the name 'Elijah' over those passages is the concept's own step. 'Send' and 'prepare the way' are in Malachi 3:1, 4:5 (I will send you), Isaiah 40:3, Mark 1:2; the Elijah passages (Malachi 4:5-6, Luke 1:17, Matthew 11:14, 17:11-12) stay under it in their own words, and Matthew 11:10, which quotes Malachi 3:1 and then says 11:14, is the text making the link.

Completeness: the name is the seven promises 'to the one who overcomes', and two are placed elsewhere (2:26 under the iron scepter, 3:5 under white clothing). Five of seven shown looks like a selection; list all seven here (the other concepts may keep them too).

concepts.name: I hold the keys
concepts.why: Name against passages: Revelation 1:18 (the keys of Death and of Hades), 9:1 and 20:1 (the key to the Abyss) are not the key of David. Isaiah 22:22 and Revelation 3:7-8 are; the other three are keys. Either rename plainly (the keys) or split the key of David from the other keys.

concepts.name: The holy city: its gates and its foundations
concepts.why: Israel and the church (Reformed, Baptist-dispensational, Catholic, Orthodox) and name against passages: the concept gives the twelve gates inscribed with the names of the tribes of Israel (Revelation 21:12, Ezekiel 48:31) and leaves out Revelation 21:14, the twelve foundations with the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb, which the same passage says; showing only one half takes a side. Isaiah 54:11-12 (sapphire foundations, gates of jewels) has no partner without Revelation 21:18-21. Only Ezekiel 40:2 and Revelation 21:10 say 'mountain', so the long name over-promises.

secondary_or_links: Order of the last things: concepts 24-69 follow Revelation's chapter order closely enough (sixth seal, Day of the LORD, distress, abomination, beasts, bowls, assembly for battle, books and thrones, kingdom, resurrection, city) to read as a timeline, and some adjacencies take a side: resurrection (59) after the books (52), thrones (53) and the kingdom (55) is the premillennial arrangement; the sixth-seal and Day-of-the-LORD concepts (25-26) before the distress (30) is one answer on tribulation and the Day of the Lord, while Matthew 24 itself puts the distress (24:21) before the darkened sun (24:29). The outline should say on the page that the concepts follow the order the books present things, not an order of events, or the end-times run should be grouped by image rather than ordered; and a thousand years (see missing) should not be left out because of the controversy.

Secondary 'Fire from heaven -> and the sky shut': Revelation 11:5-6 has fire proceeding from the witnesses' mouths, not from heaven. Rename to 'Fire consumes them, and the sky is shut' (2 Kings 1:10 and Revelation 11:5 both have fire that consumes) or drop the word 'heaven'.

Links: add the Spirit theme (concept 2 and 60 are about the Spirit carrying the seer and the breath entering; concept 19 the seven spirits). The drafter dropped Spirit as 'no concept here is about it', which is false for these three. Add the Sacrifice theme (the Lamb slain, concept 18; the altar of incense and censer, concept 47). Consider the death theme (Isaiah 25:8, Daniel 12:2, Revelation 20:13-14, 21:4 are about death swallowed up).

Concept 16 and 12 and 17 and 18 and 68 (Messiah/Christology): no change asked, but the About view should keep saying the groupings follow shared words and the texts' own quotations, not a claim of fulfilment.
Hair secondary: Daniel 7:9 and Revelation 1:14 share their wording and the grouping makes no claim; nothing to change.

The 69 concepts hold no pair that is the same sub-theme named twice, so no merge is recommended. Closest pairs: 61 (The measuring rod) and 62 (the holy city): Ezekiel 40:2-3 and Revelation 21:10, 21:15-16 are the same two scenes cut in two, but 61 also holds the temple measuring of Zechariah 2 and Revelation 11:1, so keep both and watch for duplicate verses. 52 (books) and 53 (thrones): the same court scene of Daniel 7:9-10 and Revelation 20:4, 11-12 split by image; distinct images, keep both. 43 (fire and sulfur, smoke) and 44 (worm, unquenched fire): both the unending fire of judgment, but different texts and images. 12 and 13 share Matthew 24:30 and Revelation 1:7 but the pierced one is its own sub-theme.

missing.why: Revelation 20 is cited in five concepts (thrones, image, books, dragon, gathering) yet the thousand years themselves, which the text states six times, appear nowhere as a sub-theme; the drafter dropped the note 'reign with Christ' to avoid a side. A sub-theme that only quotes the texts' words ('a thousand years', Psalm 90:4's 'a thousand years in Your sight are like a day') takes no side on how they are read, and leaving the most conspicuous number in Revelation unnamed costs credibility. Neutral: name it with the texts' words and put in nothing about when or what.

The texts' own repeated phrase, split now between the overcomer promises (2:11) and the lake of fire (21:8) without being gathered; 20:6 and 20:14 appear in no concept. Its hardness is the reason to name it, not to leave it as a stray.

The trumpet announces the Day in Joel and Zephaniah, gathers the elect in Matthew 24:31, raises the dead in 1 Corinthians 15:52 and 1 Thessalonians 4:16, and is seven in Revelation; Revelation 1:10 and 4:1 already have the trumpet voice. It is a cross-book image the outline touches only in passing (Matthew 24:31 as a secondary) and the whole gathering-and-raising run of 1 Thessalonians 4 and 1 Corinthians 15 is absent; naming only the trumpet words takes no side on the order.

missing.sub_theme: I will shake the heavens and the earth
missing.why: The shaking is in the texts' own words across prophets and Hebrews and is partly scattered (the quake of Revelation 6:12 and Joel 2:10 now only appears in the sun-and-moon concept); it holds the theme of what cannot be shaken (Hebrews 12:27-28) beside Revelation 16:18.

Revelation 5:9 and 14:3 say 'a new song'; the same words open Psalms 33, 96, 98 and Isaiah 42:10. A plain cross-book image (the song, not a reading of who sings) that completes the hymns of the heavenly scenes already here (Holy, holy, holy; Worthy is the Lamb).
